lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Here — let this man settle it. Menippus, you decide: which of us is better-looking?
lines.note: Nireus appeals to Menippus with the confidence of a man who already knows the answer.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well, who are you? I'd need to know that first, I think.
lines.note: Completely flat. No rudeness — just the obvious question.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And which is which? That part isn't obvious yet.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: Well, that's already one point to me — that I look exactly like him, and he's not nearly as remarkable as that blind poet Homer made him out to be, calling him the handsomest man at Troy. Point is, I'm the one with the pointy head and the thin hair, and the judge couldn't tell the difference between us.
lines.note: Thersites is enjoying himself enormously. He's been waiting for this for centuries.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: So — Menippus — which of us do you think is better-looking?

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Me, obviously. Son of Aglaia and Charopus. 'The most beautiful man who came to Troy.'
lines.note: Nireus quotes Homer at himself, unselfconsciously.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Yes, but you didn't come under the ground as the most beautiful, as far as I can see. The bones are the same. Your skull is distinguishable from Thersites' skull on exactly one count: yours is more fragile. It's delicate. Not what you'd call a manly skull.
lines.note: Delivered as a clinical observation. 'Not what you'd call a manly skull' is the kicker — bone-dry.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Go and ask Homer what I looked like when I was on campaign with the Achaeans.
lines.note: Nireus appeals to his literary reputation with the slightly desperate energy of someone who has been losing this argument.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Ancient history. I can only judge what you've got now. The people who were there at the time, they knew. I wasn't.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: So you're saying I'm not better-looking, even here?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Neither you nor anyone else. Down here it's equal standing and everyone looks the same.
lines.note: The running gag delivered as a simple verdict.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.note: One of the best last lines in the collection. Said with deep, quiet satisfaction.
